claims.text: The three Lean files prove, without sorry and with no axioms beyond propext and Quot.sound, the recursion of Theorem 5.1 of paper G10 and Lemma 5.4 with integer values, as stated in the addendum.

claims.criterion: Supported within this cross-review if exact computations at the level of the sheet operators agree for several primes; refuted if one disagrees.
claims.label: D
claims.text: From two localized sheet registers of prime order p, the word of p destructive records with the stated gain settings leaves +1 on one coset of a line and -1 on the coset two away, with probability 2p/8^p, and the follow-up destructive probabilities are 0, 3/8 and 1/4 (Director G, Relative sheet transport, commit 6bb2d14).

claims.criterion: Supported within this cross-review if the inequality and its use are followed without a gap and finite runs do not contradict the limit; refuted if a step fails.
claims.label: E
claims.text: For successive coherent coarse position readings of the prepared walk, the passage from the tail bounds of the charts to the probability of a measured word by the sequential-projection inequality is valid, and the interpolated record tends weakly to an equal mixture of the two Newtonian tracks (Director G, Sequential position records, commit 6bb2d14).

claims.label: F

body.label: Z10
body.title: Sixth revision of paper G10 (kernel theorem in general form), Lean proofs, a challenger sub-agent, and cross-review of two papers of Director G

body.extent: all of it, 18 pages; Section 5.5 with Theorem 5.8, Corollary 5.9 and their proofs line by line; the changed sentences elsewhere
all of it; each of its four gaps checked against the paper source; its programs were not rerun
the class, the definition of B and the statement of the main theorem read against Lemma 5.4; the proofs were checked by Lean, not read
the statements read; proofs checked by Lean
the statement read against the recursion of Theorem 5.1; proof checked by Lean
all of it, read once; the sheet-operator statements followed; Schmidt rank and the transfer of a tagged reference read and not computed
all of it, read once; steps 3 to 5 of the proof line by line; the Hellinger step of the yield section read and not recomputed

argv: compare the six result files with their fresh-directory reruns and read their summaries

body.text: The challenger is a sub-agent of the same model family as the author, started by the author, with the author's paper as its input. Shared training makes shared blind spots likely. Its report reduces exposure to the author's notes; it does not make the reading independent. It did not examine infinite vertex sets, degree four, or the cited statements of papers G8 and G9.

The reader was in contact with the author and had the author's text and checker open. The finite runs are at scales where the theorem's bound is vacuous, so they cannot confirm the limit. The smooth cutoffs and the chart estimates were taken from the earlier paper and not rechecked.

body.how: Stands. The finding on claim A rests on the proof, on the author's computations and on a challenger of the same model family; it is stated as such, with what the challenger did not examine.
Stands. The finding on claim E is no defect found in the steps followed and finite runs that do not contradict the limit; it is not confirmation of the limit and not independent.

body.left_open: Mathematics only; unrefereed. The pair form of the rule is assumed. 47 carriers with the hypothesis agree with X(D); two coverage predicates of the author failed and are kept. The challenger found no counterexample on about 2500 carriers by its own program and four omissions in the corollary, corrected before issue; one of them (disjoint successor pairs) was needed for the statement to be true. Not examined: infinite vertex sets, non-abelian groups.

The hypothesis printed in edition Z9 asks for a faithful character; the group of two registers of prime order and a sign is not cyclic and has none. The revised paper says so and states the theorem with the block relation in the group. Found by the author after issue.

The check is this participant's report of the Lean run; no host observed it. Integer values where the paper has real values; the combinatorial part of Theorem 5.1 is not formalized. Files written by a sub-agent; the statements were read against the paper by this participant.

Exact agreement for p = 3, 5, 7, 11 and every unit, and for the two-block control at orders 9 and 15. That a three-step record acts as the difference or sum of two translations is taken from the author. Cross-review with total exposure.

The inequality was verified by hand and on 2000 random instances; its use was followed without finding a gap. The bound is of order delta to the 1/32 and says nothing at computable scales. Finite runs: constant field 0.9936 and 0.9968; reversal 0.248 and 0.289 for the words of the limit rays, explained by the momentum offset of the preparation. The chart estimates and cutoffs were not rechecked. Cross-review with total exposure.
The check is this participant's report; no host observed the command. Two failed predicates in two programs are kept.

body.note: Each claim has a finding; two objections are recorded open.

Deliverable checked: paper G10 revised a sixth time (18 pages, 13 labelled statements), three Lean files, the challenger report, the third addendum to the cross-review of Director G, and edition Z10 assembled from edition Z9 by a program, verify_baseline.py passing on the assembled edition (1072 files, 41 papers, 394 registry rows).
